issues.legal_issue: A cheque issued by a person to discharge another person's fixed and acknowledged debt can be for the discharge of a debt or other liability even when described as security, where it was to be returned only upon payment and was presented after payment was not made.
material_facts: A fixed amount paid under an agreement became refundable when the agreement was cancelled, and the recipient acknowledged the debt and promised to repay it within a specified period.
The promissory note stated that the post-dated cheques were security and were to be returned when the amount was paid.
The respondent acknowledged that he had issued the cheques to the debtor for delivery to the complainant and agreed that they could be presented after a later date.
The debt was not paid by the agreed time, and the cheques were presented and dishonoured for insufficient funds.
The trial court and first appellate court found the execution of the promissory note and the respondent’s endorsement proved.
issues.conclusion: The cheques were related to an existing debt or liability and could be presented when the debt was not paid. The High Court erred in setting aside the conviction; the appellate court’s order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, a cheque must be for payment of a debt or other liability. A negotiable instrument is presumed to be supported by consideration. A cheque described as security is not thereby excluded from Section 138 where a fixed debt is acknowledged, the cheque is connected to its discharge, and it is returnable only upon payment. The Court distinguished a continuing contract or business arrangement in which no determinate amount is due when the cheque is issued. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: cheque_dishonour_prosecution and fixed_debt_acknowledged and cheque_issued_for_debt_discharge and cheque_returnable_only_after_payment and debt_unpaid_when_cheque_presented and cheque_dishonoured

predicates.cheque_dishonour_prosecution: A prosecution was brought alleging dishonour of a cheque issued for payment.
predicates.fixed_debt_acknowledged: The person liable for payment acknowledged a fixed debt that had become due.
predicates.cheque_issued_for_debt_discharge: The cheque issuer issued the cheque for delivery to the creditor in connection with discharging that debt.
predicates.cheque_returnable_only_after_payment: The parties provided that the cheque would be returned only when the debt was paid.
predicates.debt_unpaid_when_cheque_presented: The debt remained unpaid when the cheque was presented for payment.
predicates.cheque_dishonoured: The bank refused payment of the presented cheque.
predicates.cheque_dishonour_conviction_is_upheld: The conviction for cheque dishonour is upheld.

issues.definition: When a cheque-dishonour prosecution concerns a cheque issued for a fixed acknowledged debt, returnable only after payment, and the debt remains unpaid when the cheque is presented and dishonoured, the conviction is upheld.
